newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says bomb mailed from Japan.
newsitem.headline: Burma says bomb mailed from Japan.

text.p: Burma's military government on Tuesday said a bomb attack that killed the daughter of a senior army official was masterminded by anti-government groups based in Japan.
The government said in a statement the parcel bomb that exploded on Sunday night at the home of Lieutenant-General Tin Oo was sent from Japan.
"Initial investigation revealed that the terrorist bomb that exploded at Lieutenant-General Tin Oo's residence on the evening of 6 April 1997 was airmailed from Japan," said the statement.
"There are reasons to believe that the bomb plot was masterminded by some anti-Myanmar (Burma) government groups within Japan which have resorted to acts of terrorism."

There are several active exile groups in Japan and other Asian countries such as Thailand and India. Exile groups in Thailand have been blamed for previous bomb attacks in Burma but all have denied involvement in Sunday's explosion.

Cho Lei Oo, Tin Oo's 34-year old daughter, was killed in the bomb explosion on Sunday. Tin Oo is one of the four most powerful men in the government and holds the posts of Secretary Two of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council and Army Chief of Staff.
